enhanced_information: In cases of suspected congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) in a pregnant female, the drug of choice is dexamethasone. This is due to its effectiveness in reducing fetal adrenal hyperplasia and preventing virilization of the female fetus by inhibiting excess androgen production. Dexamethasone crosses the placenta and has a well-established safety profile in pregnancy, making it the preferred corticosteroid over alternatives like betamethasone, hydrocortisone, or prednisolone, which are not first-line treatments for this specific indication. The consensus supports dexamethasone as the most studied and effective option for managing CAH in pregnancy.
